forecaster_note: Wed: strong S gusts and a spike of short-period S swell — S exposures well overhead to 2x OH mess, sheltered S corners waist high, slightly more exposed ones chest to head with cleanish faces; easing PM. Thu: S swell eases, head to OH at S magnets, light S–SW AM then S/SE bump. Fri: S swell drifts SSE, persistent easterlies add lump. Sat: short-period SSE swell + E windswells, onshore, junky. — Surfline forecaster, Wed 14 Oct

wind.summary: S ~28 kph (gusts 40) at 6am, easing to ~25 by 9am; still S through the day. Rain showers at dawn.

shark.summary: Northern Beaches (Palm Beach → Manly), last 24h: 5 detections, all PALM BEACH — tagged White Shark #3494 pinged the Palm Beach receiver 5 times between 9:49pm and 10:55pm last night (newest ~7h ago). Nothing at Manly, Curl Curl, Dee Why or Long Reef. Feed is current (newest statewide detection ~2h ago, Killcare; 43 real detections statewide in 24h). DPI feed returned no features. Check the live map before paddling out.

days.label: Today
days.note: Strong S wind and a big dead-S swell spike (11.5ft @ 9s, ~2000 kJ) — Dee Why/Long Reef/Curl Curl a wind-hit mess, poor. Only sheltered North Steyne (Manly) is surfable: chest to head, cleanish. Dawn on the 4:31am low push; easing PM.
days.surfline_text: Breezy to strong southerlies and decent a spike of short period S swell. South exposures are copping the winds and swell - they'll be a well overhead to 2x OH mess so best give these a miss. Wrap will be limited for the well sheltered Sth corners - waist high. But a bit more will get into the slightly more exposed ones, with cleanish faces and maybe chest to head surf. Might be worth trading a bit of quality for a bit more size. Easing a bit for PM.

alerts: Strong S wind (gusts to ~42 kph) and heavy S swell spike — messy; rain showers at dawn

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: S swell easing; light S–SW at dawn is the window (fair), then S/SE bump from lunch. Head to OH at S magnets, chest-ish elsewhere. Go early.
days.surfline_text: Raw size and energy will have calmed down compared to Friday as mid-period S swell eases through the day and we see a little E swell. Head to OH at S magnets - with more OH sets in the morning. Sheltered S corners about waist high. AM has the best chance of clean conditions with light S to maybe SW winds. Then light to moderate S/SE'lies add some bump / wobble but it should be alrightish.

dee-why.window: AM light S/SW (7–9 kph) = best window, then S/SE onshore ~16 kph from noon. Low 5:00am (0.5m), high 11:42am. S swell easing.

long-reef.window: Dawn light S–SW, SE bump after midday. S swell easing.

curl-curl.window: Light S–SW dawn; S exposures head to overhead, north end smaller. SE lump from noon.

manly.window: Sheltered S corners about waist high, more at exposed bits. Best chance of clean in the AM before light S/SE bump.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Short-period SSE swell + small E windswells with onshore E winds — junky, waist to chest, bigger at S magnets. Dawn only. Fri 16 is also E-lumpy. (Sun 18 not yet forecast.)
days.surfline_text: Short period SSE swell is joined by some easterly windswells. Sth magnets will still be picking up the most size - in the head high plus range. Most other beaches will be waist to chest. We're still going to be battling the onshore winds - best chance for something more appealing will be in the early morning and maybe at the very S facing breaks if we get a bit of N in the wind. I think it will be pretty junky though.

dee-why.window: Sat 17: SSE short-period swell + small E windswells, E/ENE onshore 15–19 kph. Early morning only. Sun 18 not yet forecast.

long-reef.window: Waist to chest, onshore E all day; dawn at best.

curl-curl.window: Waist to chest; S end picks up most. Junky — dawn the pick.

manly.window: S magnets head high plus; Manly the likeliest for size. Onshore E — dawn only.
